name: SaleTides – Sales Insights for WooCommerce
author: saletides

sections.description:
WooCommerce’s built-in reports show you charts. SaleTides tells you what they mean.

Open SaleTides → Insights and you get a short list of what changed in your store, written in plain English:

  • “Revenue is up 23% compared with the previous 30 days. Biggest driver: Trail Runner Jacket (+$1,240).”
  • “14 repeat customers haven’t ordered in 3–6 months. Together they have spent $4,180 with you.”
  • “Organic search: google brought in $860 less than in the previous period.”
  • “Saturday is your best day, with 21% of revenue. Time emails and promotions for it.”

Everything is worked out on your own site, from your own WooCommerce orders. No account, no setup and no data leaves your store.

What you get, free

  • Insights feed: what moved revenue, average order value, traffic sources, refunds and product concentration, in plain sentences.
  • Key numbers with comparisons: revenue, net revenue after refunds, orders, average order value, items sold and customers, each compared with the previous period.
  • Sales chart: by day, week or month, with the previous period drawn alongside.
  • Repeat customers: the share of customers who order again, and how many days they take between orders.
  • Customer health: how many customers are loyal, new, at risk or lapsed.
  • Revenue by traffic source: reads the order attribution data WooCommerce already records (Google, Facebook, newsletters, direct…) and turns it into a report WooCommerce doesn’t have.
  • Top products and top customers, with guest orders grouped by email.
  • Weekly email summary (optional): last week’s numbers and insights every Monday morning.
  • Dashboard widget: the last 7 days at a glance.

Built for busy stores

SaleTides reads WooCommerce’s order tables directly with a few bounded queries instead of loading orders one by one, and caches the results for an hour. It does not rely on WooCommerce Analytics’ import tables, so there is nothing to “re-import” when they get out of date. It supports High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the older posts storage.

On very large stores, the customer figures are based on the newest 50,000 paid orders to keep the page fast; the page says so when that applies.

Want to know why?

The free insights show what changed. SaleTides shows why, who, and what to do next:

  • An AI assistant you can ask anything about your store (or connect to Claude or ChatGPT)
  • Cohort reports and customer lifetime value
  • Lifetime value by traffic source, campaign and landing page
  • Customer segments, profiles and exports
  • Refund, tax, shipping, discount and store credit reports
  • Subscriptions and abandoned carts
  • Multiple stores and team logins

Try it free for 30 days, no credit card needed. The free trial imports your newest 50,000 orders; the rest of your history is imported when you choose a plan. Using SaleTides is entirely optional: everything in this plugin works without it.

External services

This plugin does not send any data to any external service.

It contains links to saletides.com (for example “Start your free 30-day trial”). Nothing is sent when the page loads; the links only open saletides.com in your browser if you click them. They carry UTM tags that say which part of the plugin was clicked, and nothing about your store.

If you choose to create a SaleTides account and connect your store, you approve that connection on WooCommerce’s own authorization screen, and SaleTides then reads your store data through the WooCommerce REST API. That is covered by the SaleTides Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

The optional weekly email summary is sent by your own site with wp_mail(), to the address you choose.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install SaleTides from Plugins → Add New, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Activate the plugin and open SaleTides → Insights.
  4. Optional: turn on the weekly email under SaleTides → Settings.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin send my store data anywhere?

No. All numbers are calculated on your own site. Data only goes to SaleTides if you create a SaleTides account and approve the connection in WooCommerce.

Which orders are counted as sales?

Orders in WooCommerce’s “paid” statuses (Processing and Completed by default). Developers can change this with the saletides_paid_statuses filter.

How is net revenue calculated?

Revenue from paid orders in the period, minus refunds made in the same period.

Where does the traffic source data come from?

From WooCommerce’s built-in Order Attribution (WooCommerce 8.5 and later). If it is turned off, enable it under WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → Features. Orders placed before it was on have no source.

How do “loyal”, “new”, “at risk” and “lapsed” work?

Loyal: two or more orders, the latest within 90 days. New: one order, within 90 days. At risk: last order 3 to 6 months ago. Lapsed: no order for more than 6 months. Customers are grouped by billing email, so guest orders are included.

Will it slow down my site?

No. It only runs on its own admin pages, the dashboard widget and the weekly email, never on your storefront. Results are cached for an hour; use the Refresh button to recalculate.

Who can see the reports?

Users with WooCommerce’s “View WooCommerce reports” capability (Shop Managers and Administrators). Settings require “Manage WooCommerce”.
